sms.body: Beware of phishing websites which are designed to look like Internet Banking portals. Scammers are targeting people to steal sensitive information like Internet Banking credentials, mobile number and OTP to carry out fraudulent transactions. DO NOT click on suspicious links with ngrok.io/xxxxbank received via email or SMS from an unknown sender. It might look like it is from your bank and may ask you to update KYC details. Unsuspectingly clicking on the link will give the fraudster access to your device to steal confidential details and use your account to carry out fraudulent transactions. To report an incident, please call 18002586465 / 18001024734. - StanChart

sms.body: प्रिय भागधारक , आपल्या बँकेच्या व्यवसायात वाढ व्हावी यासाठी आपले संचालक मंडळ, व्यवस्थापन व शाखा विविध प्रकारचे उपक्रम राबवत असतात. व्यवस्थापन व संचालक मंडळाच्या संयुक्त विचारांती बँकेच्या दहा भौगोलिक विभाग करण्यात आले असून प्रत्येक विभागाची जबाबदारी एका अधिकाऱ्याला देण्यात आली आहे. सदर विभागात आतापर्यंत सुमारे 40 पेक्षा जास्त असे कार्यक्रम त्या त्या विभागात झाले असून, पुढेही असे कार्यक्रम आयोजित करण्यात येणार आहेत. सदर कार्यक्रमामुळे बँकेची प्रसिध्दी व व्यवसाय वाढीसाठी मदत होणार आहे. जनसंपर्क अधिकारी -BCCB

part.text: Can u identify spam messages and delete those

part.name: text.txt
part.text:
I cannot directly "identify spam messages and delete those" in your personal accounts (like email or messages). My capabilities as an AI do not extend to accessing or managing your private data for security and privacy reasons.​
However, I can ​provide you with information and strategies to help you identify and manage spam messages yourself.​
How to Identify Spam Messages:​
Spam messages often have common characteristics:​ Suspicious Sender:​ Unknown or unusual email addresses/phone numbers.​Generic sender names (e.g., "Customer Service," "Support Team")​Email addresses that don't match the company they claim to be from (e.g., "amazon-support@randomdomain.xyz" instead of "support@amazon.com").​Urgent or Threatening Language:​ "Act now or your account will be suspended!"​"You've won a lottery, claim your prize immediately!"​Threats of legal action, fines, or account closure.​Requests for Personal Information:​ Asking for passwords, credit card numbers, bank details, Aadhaar numbers, or OTPs. Legitimate organizations rarely ask for this information via email or text.​Too Good to Be True Offers:​ Unbelievable discounts, free prizes, or huge lottery winnings that you never entered.​Poor Grammar and Spelling:​ Many spam messages, especially from overseas, contain numerous grammatical errors and typos.​Suspicious Links or Attachments:​ Links that don't match the displayed text (hover over them to see the actual URL).​Attachments from unknown senders, especially if they are executables (.exe), zip files, or unusual document types.​Generic Greetings:​ "Dear Customer," "Dear User," instead of addressing you by name.​Unexpected Messages:​ Messages about accounts, orders, or services you don't have or weren't expecting.​ How to Manage and Delete Spam Messages (General Advice):​
The steps to delete spam depend on where you're receiving them:​
1. Email Spam:​ Mark as Spam/Junk:​ Most email providers (Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo Mail) have a "Report spam" or "Move to Junk" button. This helps train the email filter to catch similar messages in the future.​Block Sender:​ You can often block specific senders so their emails go directly to spam or are rejected.​Unsubscribe (with caution):​ If it's a legitimate marketing email you no longer want, look for an "unsubscribe" link at the bottom. ​Be very cautious about unsubscribing from obvious spam, as it can confirm your email address is active and lead to more spam.​Delete:​ Once marked as spam, you can usually delete them from your spam/junk folder. Many providers automatically delete messages from this folder after a certain period.​Create Filters:​ You can set up rules or filters to automatically move emails from specific senders or with certain keywords to your spam folder or trash.​ 2. SMS/Text Message Spam:​ Block Number:​ On most smartphones, you can open the message, tap the sender's number, and choose "Block" or "Block & Report Spam."​Report to Carrier:​ In India, you can report spam SMS to your telecom provider (Jio, Airtel, Vodafone Idea) by forwarding the message to ​1909​. This is a regulatory service to combat unwanted commercial communication.​Delete:​ Simply delete the message.​Don't Click Links or Call Numbers:​ Never click on suspicious links or call numbers from spam texts.​ 3. WhatsApp/Messaging App Spam:​ Block and Report:​ WhatsApp and similar apps allow you to block and report users who send spam or unsolicited messages. This helps the platform take action against them.​Don't Share Personal Info:​ Be wary of messages asking for OTPs, bank details, or personal information.​ Important Security Practices:​ Never click on suspicious links or open unknown attachments.​ They can contain malware or lead to phishing websites.​Never reply to spam messages.​ This confirms your email address or phone number is active.​Use strong, unique passwords​ for all your online accounts.​Enable two-factor authentication (2FA)​ wherever possible.​Keep your software and operating system updated​ to protect against known vulnerabilities.​Use reputable antivirus/antimalware software.​ If you have a specific message you're unsure about, you can describe it to me (without revealing any personal information), and I can give you an opinion on whether it sounds like spam.​
